subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, min commit & tax allocation (Acme Health)
messages:

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com

Subject: Draft order form and a few commercial clarifications

Hi Dana / Kevin —

Thanks again for taking the demo last week. Attached is the current draft Order Form (draft_orderform_v3.pdf) that aligns to the MSA terms we discussed. Before we move to signature we need to align a few commercial items so legal/procurement can sign off cleanly:

- Invoicing cadence: the draft shows one quarterly invoice for committed capacity. You mentioned preferring split invoices tied to usage — can you confirm whether you need monthly invoices, or a split structure (advance + usage reconciliation)?
- Minimum commit: the Order Form lists a 3-month minimum commit at the committed throughput level. Please confirm if that is acceptable or if Acme requires a shorter initial trial period.
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30. You indicated Net 45 in the call — please confirm if Net 45 is a hard requirement.
- Taxes: we currently price fees exclusive of taxes and have the customer responsible for VAT/GST when applicable. If Acme requires Redwood to collect VAT (EU entities), we need the correct tax registration info or a tax-exempt certificate.

If it helps, we can propose an invoice split (advance for committed capacity + monthly usage reconciliation) and Net 45 to match your cadence — I wanted to check first before circulating to Legal.

Attached: draft_orderform_v3.pdf (redlines welcome).

Next steps: if you can respond to the four items above by EOD Thursday, we’ll update the Order Form and route to DocuSign.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Draft order form and a few commercial clarifications

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick answers from Procurement so you can iterate:

1) Invoicing cadence: Acme needs split invoices. Prefer: an advance invoice for the committed baseline (quarterly) and monthly reconciliation invoices for any overage/usage. We need line items separated so our AP can map to POs.
2) Minimum commit: we are comfortable with a 1-month initial committed trial (we often do a short pilot before committing long-term). Can you provide a 30-day pilot pricing row?
3) Net terms: Net 45 is our standard for new vendors; Net 30 is unlikely to be accepted by Finance.
4) Taxes: Acme is a US entity for this contract; we do not expect Redwood to collect VAT. That said, if Redwood invoices from a non-US entity, we may require tax documentation.

Attached is our standard procurement checklist — it highlights PO number, invoice splitting, and certificate requirements.

We can review the updated Order Form on Thursday afternoon (we have a procurement sync then).

Best,
Dana Wells
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the checklist. I’m looping in Finance and Legal touchpoints and proposing an approach that should be acceptable to both sides:

- Invoicing: we’ll split invoices into two lines: (A) Committed baseline — invoiced in advance on a quarterly cadence, (B) Usage/overage — invoiced monthly with reconciliation. Each invoice will include the Acme PO number and line-item mapping.
- Pilot row: we’ll add a 30-day pilot row with a reduced rate for the initial month. That pilot will be explicitly non-cancellable and will convert to the committed baseline unless you notify us within the pilot window.
- Net terms: we can accept Net 45 for this agreement. Please confirm the payment remittance details we should include.
- Taxes: we will surface tax-exclusive pricing with a tax section. If you are invoiced from Redwood Inc. (US entity) then we won’t collect VAT. If, for operational reasons, billing comes from a non-US Redwood entity, we’ll need a tax form or documentation to ensure correct handling.

I’ve attached a proposed payment schedule (proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx) with the advance/usage split and sample invoice dates. Happy to tweak if your AP has specific cutoffs.

If this is acceptable, Olga will push an updated Order Form v4 and route to Legal for a clean redline before we send to you for signature.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Quick Finance note —

I reviewed Lauren’s payment schedule. A pragmatic compromise to protect revenue recognition while meeting Acme’s AP needs: invoice 60% of the first quarter committed baseline as an initial advance (one-time at kickoff), then invoice the remaining 40% pro rata across the next two monthly invoices for that quarter. After quarter one, revert to: advance quarterly invoice for baseline + monthly usage reconciliation.

On taxes: for US invoicing there’s no VAT concern. If we must invoice from a non-US entity for contractual reasons, include language that the customer is responsible for any local consumption taxes and provide Redwood with tax exemption docs if available.

Deal tracking: RDW-ACME-10234 — please confirm so Sales Ops can queue the revenue schedule.

—Rishi
